Cyber Attack Disrupts Ghana’s Power Grid and Payment Systems

A widespread cyber attack targeting Ghana’s national infrastructure has disrupted electricity supply and digital payments across the country, with Electricity Co Of Ghana Ltd among the affected entities. The incident, which began early Thursday, is ongoing, and authorities are working to contain the impact amid rising concerns from businesses, consumers, and trade unions.

Electricity outages have been reported in Accra, Kumasi, Takoradi, and several regional centers, halting operations in banks, supermarkets, and small businesses that rely on point-of-sale terminals and mobile money transfers. The Ghana Chamber of Commerce estimated that over 60% of urban businesses experienced disruptions in the first twelve hours of the attack.

Electricity Co Of Ghana Ltd issued a statement confirming "unprecedented network interruptions impacting supply and customer service operations nationwide," and urged customers to conserve power where possible. The company’s spokesperson, Kwame Mensah, said technicians are “working round the clock to restore normalcy” but warned that “full resolution may take time as digital control systems remain compromised.”

Telecommunications services have also been intermittently affected, disrupting internet connectivity and hampering remote work and online transactions. “We are seeing a ripple effect through the economy, with particular pressure on retail and logistics,” said Efua Asare, an analyst at Kwansema Advisory. “Many businesses are reverting to cash, but payment systems have been unreliable throughout the day.”

The Ghana National Trade Union Congress called for urgent government intervention, citing the risk of lost wages and halted production lines. “Workers in affected sectors need assurances that their livelihoods will be protected during this crisis,” said General Secretary Kofi Boateng.

The Ministry of National Security has launched an investigation and is collaborating with international cyber experts. In a press briefing, Minister Nana Owusu said, “We urge calm as we pursue all avenues to restore critical services and identify the perpetrators.”

As of late Thursday, there was no official estimate of when full services would be restored. The attack marks one of the most significant cyber threats to Ghana’s economic infrastructure in recent years.
